name: Battle of Puebla
note: The accounts do not give compass directions or distances, so the forts, the city, the maguey field and every formation are placed by judgement on the sides the story needs. The accounts say the French columns joined and split into three; the plan draws the zouaves and a second column, and a third column where it reaches the east side. The accounts do not say who made up the second column or the Mexican force on the French left, which is not drawn.

phases.title: The French form up below the forts
phases.text: Lorencez drew up an attack column of zouaves and guns, with a reserve behind it and a convoy guarded on the flank. The forts of Loreto and Guadalupe were held by Negrete's division, and Mexican cavalry stood on the French right.
phases.quote: At half past eleven Lorencez arranged an attack column made up of two battalions of zouaves

phases.title: The French halt and shell the forts
phases.text: The zouaves climbed towards Guadalupe and, when opposite it, halted and planted their artillery. The guns fired on both forts, and Zaragoza gave orders for them to be reinforced.
phases.quote: The French division advanced and when opposite the Guadalupe fort, halted and planted its artillery to fire upon the Guadalupe and the Loreto forts.

phases.title: The French meet two Mexican battalions halfway up
phases.text: The zouaves climbed with little opposition and had gone halfway when two Mexican battalions met them, exchanged shots with the sharpshooters and returned to their position. Berriozábal was ordered to reinforce the two hills.
phases.quote: They had completed half of the ascent when they were met by two battalions of Mexican infantry, which after exchanging shots with French sharpshooters, returned to their position.

phases.title: The column turns between the forts and is fired on
phases.text: The ascending column turned diagonally to the right, as if to go between the two forts, and both forts fired on the French troops. Mexican infantry under cover of the maguey field kept firing as well.
phases.quote: The ascending column now turned diagonally towards the right, as if going between the two forts, and the two forts now took advantage of the opportunity to fire upon the French troops.

phases.title: The French retreat and a second column comes up
phases.text: The zouaves retreated and the Mexicans pursued them. The pursuit stopped when another French column came to support the retreating troops.
phases.quote: the French retreated and were pursued by Mexican forces, but the pursuit was given up when another French column came to the support of the retreating troops.

phases.title: The second attack, from the north and the east
phases.text: The two French columns pushed on together towards the Guadalupe and Resurrection chapel, joined and split into three. The attack was more vigorous. Diaz came up with part of his brigade and two guns.
phases.quote: The two French columns now pushed on together towards the Guadalupe and Resurrection chapel.

phases.title: The columns are repulsed
phases.text: The columns that went up from the north were routed. Diaz, with part of his brigade and two guns, checked and drove away the French columns marching against the Mexican positions.
phases.quote: The two columns which attempted an assault on the hill from the north again were completely routed.

phases.title: The third column is defeated on the east side
phases.text: The third French column reached the east side just as the other two were being repulsed, and it was also defeated there.
phases.quote: The third French column which reached the east side just as the others were repulsed was also defeated.

phases.title: The Mexican cavalry charge and the French withdraw
phases.text: The Mexican cavalry charged the remaining French and prevented them from reorganising for further assaults. The two armies faced each other until seven in the evening, when the French returned to their camp.
phases.quote: The Mexican cavalry then charged upon the remaining French and prevented their reorganization for further assaults.
